subject: Tobit
note: Evidence for Tobit's Bible figure page. His whole record is the Book of Tobit (14 chapters), which is not in the BSB: every line from it is quoted from the World English Bible (shared/web-world-english-bible.txt, book code TOB), whose text is the shorter Greek form (it has 4:7-19 and a short chapter 5, as the Vatican/Alexandrian text does). Where Jerome's Latin differs (the dog's tail, the reason for the blindness, his age at death) it is quoted from the Douay-Rheims and named as such. The page has 12 moments, no miracles section (the healing and the demon are the angel's work and are told among the moments, as Martha's page tells Lazarus), no feasts (no calendar checked gives Tobit a day), and one section of his own, 'His book' (which Bibles hold it, and whether it is history, each side in its own words), as the task asked. Every quotation is in tobit.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in design/saints-hub/sources/people/tobit/ (gitignored).

life.text: Tobit of the tribe of Naphtali, carried captive from Thisbe in Galilee in the days of Enemessar.

Alone of his tribe he went to Jerusalem at the feasts; first fruits to the priests; a tenth to the Levites; a second tenth spent in Jerusalem each year; a third given as Deborah his father's mother commanded, because he was left an orphan.

Married Anna of his own family; father of Tobias; kept from the bread of the Gentiles; purchasing agent of Enemessar; left ten talents of silver with Gabael at Rages of Media; under Sennacherib the roads to Media were troubled.

Gave bread to the hungry and garments to the naked; buried his people thrown out on the wall of Nineveh; buried in secret those Sennacherib killed; was reported, hid and fled; everything taken but Anna and Tobias; the king killed by two of his sons within fifty-five days; Sarchedonus set Achiacharus, Tobit's brother Anael's son, over the accounts, and Achiacharus asked for Tobit.
The Pentecost dinner, the strangled man, 'Before I had tasted anything, I sprang up', the burial after sunset, the neighbours' mockery.
Slept by the courtyard wall, sparrows' warm dung fell into his open eyes, white films; physicians did not help; Achiacharus nourished him until he went into Elymais.
Anna wove cloth for wages; the kid; 'Where are your alms and your righteous deeds?'
Tobit's prayer to die; the same day Sarah in Ecbatana, seven husbands killed by Asmodaeus before they lay with her, mocked by her father's maids, prays; both heard; Raphael sent to heal both.

Tobit's advice to Tobias (alms, the negative Golden Rule 4:15, wages the same day 4:14, idleness the mother of famine 4:13, counsel 4:18); the hiring of Azarias for a drachma a day; 'May his angel go with you'; the dog; Anna's weeping; 'a good angel will go with him'.

The fish at the Tigris; Raguel's house; 'You are the son of an honest and good man'; the marriage; the demon fled to the uppermost parts of Egypt and was bound; Tobias and Sarah's prayer; Raguel dug a grave 'Lest he also should die' and had it filled; fourteen days of wedding feast.
Raphael fetched the money from Gabael (the bags with their seals); Tobit counted every day; Anna watched the road and ate no bread; 'Hold your peace. Don't worry. He is in good health.'

The homecoming: Anna ran to her son; Tobit stumbled at the door; the gall; the white films peeled away; his blessing; he met Sarah at the gate of Nineveh and those who saw him marvelled; Achiacharus came to the seven-day feast.

Raphael's wages (half of all); his teaching on alms; 'When you buried the dead, I was with you'; 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels'; 'Write in a book all the things which have been done'; they saw him no more.
Tobit's prayer of rejoicing: 'For he scourges, and shows mercy. He leads down to the grave, and brings up again.'

Blind at fifty-eight, sight restored after eight years; called his son and six grandsons; told them to leave Nineveh because of Jonah's prophecy; foretold Jerusalem's ruin and return; 'Bury me decently, and your mother with me'; the Ahikar example (14:10); died in bed at 158; Tobias buried him magnificently and Anna with him, moved to Ecbatana, died at 127, heard of Nineveh's fall.

In Jerome's Latin (Douay): the dog ran before and wagged its tail (11:9); the trial permitted as an example of patience 'as also of holy Job' (2:12); 'because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee' (12:13); he lived 102 years (14:2).
life.source: Douay-Rheims, Tobias 2, 11, 12, 14 (drbo.org). The Catholic Encyclopedia confirms the dog's tail is in the Vulgate alone.

life.text: In the Vulgate and some Hebrew texts father and son are both Tobias; the Greek calls the father Tobit/Tobeit; tobi 'my good', Tobias 'Yahweh is good'.

Enemessar is Shalmaneser, Sarchedonus is Esarhaddon, Achiacharus is Ahikar; the reference in 14:10 shows acquaintance with an Ahikar story; composed probably between 200 and 50 BC; 'It may be reckoned among the most delightful of short stories.'; 'A late Jewish work, never received into the Jewish canon'.
life.source: Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), 'Tobit, Book of', by Crawford Howell Toy.

life.text: 2 Kings says Tiglath-pileser carried away all the land of Naphtali.
life.source: 2 Kings 15:29 (BSB); the Catholic Encyclopedia names this among 'certain historical difficulties' (Theglathphalasar III, not Salmanasar).

life.text: Rembrandt painted the story several times. Commons holds, under his name: Tobit and Anna with the Kid (1626, Rijksmuseum); Anna and the Blind Tobit (c. 1630); a Tobit and Anna with the kid of 1645 (Rembrandt and workshop); Tobias Healing his Father (Staatsgalerie Stuttgart).
life.source: Wikimedia Commons file pages for each painting.

said.text: Ambrose: 'Tobit also clearly portrayed in his life true virtue, when he left the feast and buried the dead...'
said.source: Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy, Book 3, chapter 16 (NPNF 2-10, shared/npnf210.txt).

said.text: Augustine on Tobit and Anna: the better light; the son's hand and the father's.
said.source: Augustine, Sermon 38 on the New Testament, on Matthew 20:30 (NPNF 1-6, shared/npnf106.txt).

tidbits.text: Raphael = 'God has healed'; named in the Septuagint only in Tobit; of the seven archangels only Gabriel, Michael and Raphael are named in the canonical Scriptures; the others from Enoch and apocryphal sources; feast of St Raphael 24 October.
Jerome translated Tobit with a speaker of Chaldee and Hebrew, in 'one day's hasty labour', dictating the Latin to a secretary.
tidbits.source: Jerome, preface to Tobit and Judith, as given in NPNF 2-6.

tidbits.text: Five Tobit manuscripts at Qumran: 4Q196 (papyrus), 4Q197, 4Q198, 4Q199 in Aramaic; 4Q200 in Hebrew (Fitzmyer, DJD 19).
tidbits.source: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library, manuscript pages 4Q196-1 to 4Q200-1 (sources/people/tobit/dss-tobit-manuscripts.txt).

tidbits.text: Luther: Judith 'eine gute / ernste /dapffere Tragedien', Tobias 'eine feine liebliche / gottselige Comedien'; 'Jsts ein Geschicht / so ists ein fein heilig Geschicht...'; the book 'nützlich vnd gut zu lesen'.
tidbits.source: Luther, Vorrede auffs Buch Tobie, Luther-Bibel 1545, at zeno.org. Our translations.

tidbits.text: The 1549 marriage service: 'as thou diddest sende thy Aungell Raphaell to Thobie, and Sara, the daughter of Raguel, to their great comfort'.
tidbits.source: Book of Common Prayer 1549, Solemnization of Matrimony (justus.anglican.org via the Wayback Machine; the site's own copy answers 403).

tidbits.text: Ambrose's De Tobia: sermons on the story of Tobias, chiefly against usury.

canon.text: Catholic: deuterocanonical; in the lists of Hippo 393, Carthage 397 and 419, Innocent I 405, Augustine 397; settled for Catholics by Trent, Session IV, 8 April 1546; 'its place in the Christian Canon of Holy Writ is undoubted'. Until recently no question among Catholics of its historicity; historical difficulties blamed on the imperfect text; the objections 'mere conjectures'.
canon.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1912), 'Tobias', Canonicity and Historical worth.

canon.text: Orthodox: Confession of Dositheus (Synod of Jerusalem 1672), question 3, names Tobit among 'genuine parts of Scripture'. Philaret's Longer Catechism, questions 34-36: such books are not in the Hebrew, and Athanasius says they were appointed 'to be read by proselytes who are preparing for admission into the Church'.
canon.source: crivoice.org (Robertson 1899 translation); Schaff, Creeds of Christendom vol. 2.

canon.text: Protestant: Thirty-Nine Articles, Article VI (the Church reads 'for example of life and instruction of manners', not to establish doctrine; lists the Book of Tobias); Westminster Confession 1.3 (Apocrypha of no authority).

calendars.text: No day for Tobit in the 1916 Roman Martyrology; its index entry 'Tobias, St., M Nov. 2' is a martyr of Sebaste under Licinius (with Carterius, Styriacus and companions).

No Tobit in the Calendarium Romanum 1969, USCCB 2026, Church of England calendar, LFF 2022, LSB, ELCA or the Coptic calendar files on disk. St Raphael: 24 October in the Roman calendar from 1921; since 1969 with Michael and Gabriel on 29 September.
calendars.source: shared/calendarium-romanum-1969-ocr.txt (lines on 'Raphaelis ... ab anno 1921'); usccb-2026cal.txt (29 September).

calendars.text: Orthodox: no day for Tobit found (OCA, OrthodoxWiki, Russian Wikipedia as leads). Raphael is kept with the archangels on 8 November; the OCA describes his icon leading Tobias, who carries a fish.
calendars.source: OCA, Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the Other Bodiless Powers.

calendars.text: Church of England: Common Worship Daily Prayer canticle 44, A Song of Tobit (Tobit 13.1,3,4-6a). Episcopal: Tobit 6:1-6 is a lesson for Hugh of Lincoln (17 November) and Tobit 12:8-10 for Elizabeth of Hungary (19 November).

could_not_verify: Whether the current (2004) Roman Martyrology names Tobit: not on disk and not fetched; the page claims only what the 1916 edition and the other calendars checked show ('No church calendar we checked').
A pronunciation source (Wiktionary gives none for Tobit), so the page has no 'Pronounced' fact.
Britannica has no article on Tobit at the addresses tried; the 'story that teaches' view is given through the Jewish Encyclopedia and Luther, not a modern encyclopedia.
The dates of the Qumran copies (the Leon Levy pages were read only for their titles and languages), so the page gives none.

Numbers against the WEB: eight years blind (14:2), three tenths (1:7-8), ten talents (1:14; 4:20); 158 (14:11), 127 for Tobias (14:14), six grandsons (14:3), fifty-five days (1:21).

Jerome's preface (NPNF 6), the Jewish Encyclopedia's 200 to 50 BC and 'most delightful of short stories', the Catholic Encyclopedia's Hippo 393 and Carthage 397, the 1916 Martyrology's Tobias of Sebaste under Licinius (2 November), LFF 2022's Tobit readings on 17 and 19 November, the OCA icon note (Raphael leading Tobias with the fish), Augustine's 'God is angry with him'.

A scholar read the book aloud in Hebrew, and Jerome dictated to a secretary: “one day's hasty labour”.' (the preface: an interpreter expressed the Chaldee in Hebrew words).
